newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik group threatens to shoot UN hostages.
newsitem.headline: Tajik group threatens to shoot UN hostages.

text.p: An unidentified armed group who seized 15 hostages in Tajikistan, including eight foreign United Nations military observers, on Friday threatened to shoot them if their demands were not met within two days.

A U.N. source in the capital Dushanbe told Reuters the group seized a five-car column of U.N. personnel and four Islamic opposition officials 70 km (40 miles) east of Dushanbe. They demanded the armed Islamic opposition free the brother of a rebel chief who joined forces with the government last month.

The group also demanded that Russian frontier guards, who have acted as peacekeepers in four years of Tajik civil war, provide a safe corridor for fighters loyal to the turncoat commander to join the hostage-takers from their bases across the Afghan border.
If their demands were not met by 2 p.m. (0900 GMT) on Sunday, they said, they would shoot the hostages and detonate 30 bombs which had been planted in Dushanbe.
The number of hostage-takers was not known. Their demands suggested they belonged to the group led by the guerrilla leader who defected to the government side.

U.N. military observers have already twice this month been subject to beatings and mock executions. The two earlier incidents were at the hands of Tajik government soldiers. The U.N. mission to Tajikistan fields 96 military observers in the republic and had its mandate renewed for four months last week.
